q: What is the CBAM default value for stainless steel from India?
title: CBAM default value: Indian stainless steel
short: Between 6.480 and 6.530 t CO2e per tonne for Indian stainless steel, depending on the product. Flat-rolled stainless under CN 7219 and 7220 is 6.490 or 6.500, bars and wire 6.480, and ingots 6.530. Direct emissions only, plus the 10% mark-up in 2026.
audience: Indian stainless steel sheet, coil, bar, wire and pipe exporters

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne
ul: CN 7219 flat-rolled, 600 mm and wider: 6.490 hot-rolled, 6.500 cold-rolled
CN 7221 and 7222 bars and rods: 6.480, cold-formed 6.530

p: The listed values are increased by a mark-up: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027 and 30% from 2028. Goods imported in 2026 always take the 2026 mark-up.

Stainless needs ferro-chrome and ferro-nickel, and those carry their own embedded emissions as precursors. If your alloy suppliers can give you their figures, your actual value can fall well below the default.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.

sources.label: European Commission, Default values definitive period (Excel, version 2 of 6 August 2026), India sheet; legally binding values in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740 correcting (EU) 2025/2621
European Commission, Guidance No. 3, CBAM methods for the calculation of emissions embedded in goods (14 August 2026), section 4.10
